div.head: ECf 32 B 12a
div.ab: Fundata enim erat olim et edificata ad instar et ad modum et in memoriam ueteris magne Troie; et usque in hodiernum diem leges et iura, dignitates, libertates regiasque consuetudines antique magne Troie in se continet.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 657 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 B …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints the words borrowed from William fitz Stephen in smaller type; his margin names the source (Will. f. Steph.).

note.seg: Brutus ad Tamensem condidit ciuitatem Troiam nouam; Galfr. I 17; vgl. I 11. Nochmals u. 35, 1 A 2
Brutus ad Tamensem condidit ciuitatem Troiam nouam; Galfr. I 17; cf. I 11. Again below, 35, 1 A 2

Londonia a Troianis condita, unde et adhuc antiquis eisdem utuntur legibus et communibus institutis; Will. f. Steph. Diese Sätze benutzt die Guildhall im 14. 15. Jh.; Mon. Gildh. I 61. Die Londoner hielten sich um 1190 quietos de theloneo a tempore quo Roma fundata; Jocelin Brakelond. p. 56

Londonia a Troianis condita, unde et adhuc antiquis eisdem utuntur legibus et communibus institutis; Will. f. Steph. The Guildhall uses these sentences in the 14th and 15th centuries; Mon. Gildh. I 61. Around 1190 the Londoners held themselves quietos de theloneo a tempore quo Roma fundata; Jocelin Brakelond. p. 56

div.ab: For it was once founded and built after the likeness and in the manner and in memory of ancient great Troy; and to this day it contains in itself the laws and rights, dignities, liberties and royal customs of ancient great Troy.

note.seg: Ebd. London 41. 60.a; Troja; s. u. 35,1 A 2. Ein Menschenalter vor dem Verf. schrieb Benoit de Ste. More den Roman de Troie. Über gemalte Trojaner in einer Prälatenwohnung s. Mortet Mél. Bémont 110f. London beschuldigte 1388 Nikolaus Brembre, er habe zum lebenslänglichen Mayor und Herzog von Troja steigen wollen; Pauli Gesch. v. Engl. IV 580. — enim fehlt — cons. ant. m. Troge Rs

Ibid. London 41. 60.a; Troja; see below, 35,1 A 2. A generation before the author, Benoit de Ste. More wrote the Roman de Troie. On painted Trojans in a prelate's residence see Mortet Mél. Bémont 110f. In 1388 London accused Nicholas Brembre of having wished to rise to be mayor for life and duke of Troy; Pauli Gesch. v. Engl. IV 580. — enim lacking — cons. ant. m. Troge Rs
